articleTitle: Why Getting Out of Bed When You Can't Sleep Actually Works
imageHeadline: Can't sleep? Getting out of bed retrains your brain
imageSubtext: Why stimulus control—a proven CBT-I technique—actually works
pinTitle: Why Getting Out of Bed When You Can't Sleep Works (Stimulus Control Explained)
pinDescription: Lying awake in bed trains your brain to associate it with frustration, not sleep. Stimulus control—a core part of cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia—breaks that pattern by having you leave the bedroom when sleep doesn't come. Learn how this evidence-based technique rebuilds the mental link between bed and rest.
